subject: chemistry-1
question: Which statement about the complete ionic and net ionic equations for AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq) -> AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq) is accurate?

options.text: The net ionic equation lists all four ions, since each of them is dissolved in water
The net ionic equation drops Ag+ and Cl-, since ions that form a solid are not written
The net ionic equation drops the spectator ions Na+ and NO3-, leaving Ag+ + Cl- -> AgCl(s)
The complete ionic equation writes AgCl as separate Ag+ and Cl- ions in solution

explanation:
In the complete ionic equation, soluble strong electrolytes are written as dissociated ions while the insoluble product AgCl is written as an intact solid. Na+ and NO3- appear unchanged on both sides, so they are spectator ions and cancel, leaving Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> AgCl(s). The net ionic equation isolates the chemical change that actually occurs, which is why it is the standard representation for precipitation and neutralization reactions.

ELI-10: Write out every dissolved ion first, but keep the insoluble solid together because it is not dissociated. Then cross off any ion that appears identically on both sides; it entered and left unchanged, so it did nothing. Here Na+ and NO3- cancel, and what survives is the silver ion joining the chloride ion to form solid AgCl.
